review.summary: Attempt 2 fixes the important findings from attempt 1. Added components, properties, union branches, parameters, bodies, responses, media types and operations are now scanned against the same keyword sets the compare methods use. operation_added binds the whole operation, source_removed carries nativeBindings, and an in-place change to one union branch is scoped. The evidence covers source e26a1db…: airs_drift --check, 42 drift tests (37 before, plus 5 new), and --require-through-phase 25, all exit 0. Some fail-closed gaps remain. For a newly added source, only operations and components are scanned. Document-level webhooks, x- extensions, unknown info keys and component sections outside the known set are missed, although plan:290-292 names webhooks. Whole subtrees emitted as type_changed or constraint_changed are also not scanned. Both medium findings, no blockers or high findings. Total 43.5/50, which passes the chunk threshold.

findings.description: For a new source, compare_sources only scans operations and components (979-985). Several things in a new source are never inspected: document residual keys (document_model 'document', for example webhooks or root x-*), unknown info keys, component sections outside COMPONENT_SECTIONS (callbacks, links, headers, pathItems), and securitySchemes. They come out as additive source_added, although plan:290-292 says webhooks and x- extensions must fail closed. Existing sources do fail on the same keys (compare 572-578, compare_info 604-605, compare_components 637-639).
findings.required_fix: In the old-is-None branch, fail when comparison.new['document'] is non-empty, when info has keys outside INFO_ANNOTATIONS|{version,license}, or when a component section is not in COMPONENT_SECTIONS. Scan securitySchemes for x-* keys. Extend test_added_source_is_scanned_too with webhooks, a root x- extension and a components.callbacks case.

findings.description: Some branches emit a whole new subtree as type_changed or constraint_changed without going through scan_schema: anyOf/oneOf added to an existing schema (701-703), items/additionalProperties changing from non-dict to dict (706-710), allOf/prefixItems length changes (711-716), an added media or parameter schema (882-883, 939-941), and $ref replaced by an inline schema (859-864). A discriminator, not or x-* inside such a subtree is reported as breaking instead of failing closed. Being reported as breaking keeps the risk visible to reviewers, but it is inconsistent with the scans just added.
findings.required_fix: Whenever these emits carry a new side that is not MISSING, run scan_schema (or scan_parameter/scan_media) on it first, for example by mapping type_changed/constraint_changed to scan_schema when the pointer is a schema position. Add tests that put discriminator inside a newly added anyOf and not inside a $ref→inline replacement.

findings.description: operation_removed still binds old={'operationId'} only. The symmetric fix suggested in attempt 1 was not applied, so two different removed operations with the same operationId share a change id.
findings.required_fix: Bind old=old[key], or a digest of it, and add a test that the removal id changes when the removed operation's body differs.

findings.description: scan_component ignores the securitySchemes and examples sections, so an added security scheme with x-* or unclassified keys comes out as additive component_added.
findings.required_fix: Scan added securitySchemes against a known key set (type, scheme, bearerFormat, in, name, flows, openIdConnectUrl, description) and fail on anything else.

evidence: The checks file (attempt-02.checks.json) records source_sha256 e26a1db4… with passed=true; I grepped it for non-zero exit codes and timeouts and found none.
checks.json:2303-2320: `airs_drift.py --check` exit 0, 'pinned baseline verified; ledger current; baseline self-compare unchanged'.
checks.json:2322-2352: test_airs_drift ran 42 tests OK, including the new AddedContentFailsClosedTests (5 tests).
checks.json:2269-2300: `git diff --exit-code b66133892b… -- crates/scm-sdk Cargo.* LICENSE NOTICE` exit 0, so the SDK was not mutated.
airs_drift.py:113-119 and 407-411: SCHEMA_KNOWN/PARAMETER_KNOWN/MEDIA_KNOWN are shared with the compare methods, and ADDED_SCANS dispatches a scan from emit() (430-431).

airs_drift.py:448-524: the recursive scans cover properties, items, additionalProperties, propertyNames, unions, parameters, bodies, responses, media types, and operation residual/pathResidual (callbacks, deprecated).
airs_drift.py:795: operation_added now uses new=new[key]; test_airs_drift.py:451-460 shows that different responses produce different ids.
airs_drift.py:963-973: source_removed carries deduplicated nativeBindings; test at test_airs_drift.py:462-465.
airs_drift.py:766-771: a single in-place branch change recurses via compare_schema; test_airs_drift.py:467-477 asserts constraint_changed at /maxLength.
airs_drift.py:977-985: a new source scans only operations and components. The document residual and info are unchecked, which is the basis of the first finding.
CLASSIFIER_VERSION bumped to 2 (airs_drift.py:37), and the ledger regenerates current per the --check output.
limitations: Read-only review: I did not run any tests or tools myself. Execution evidence comes only from the recorded checks file.
I sampled the 3278-line checks file and grepped the rest for failures and timeouts rather than reading all of it.

I did not re-audit check_phase.py, test_management_phases.py or the vendor 0.86.0 bytes beyond the recorded passing checks; the attempt 1 review already accepted them, and this attempt's changes are concentrated in airs_drift.py and its tests.
The webhooks and type_changed-subtree gaps were found by reading the code; I did not reproduce them with a run.
No remote CI or live pan.dev refresh was examined.
